title: Prototype structured retrieval capsules for durable Markdown
description: Follow-up to TASK-261. Define a small human-readable Retrieval capsule section for durable Markdown, add it without rewriting body prose to a representative set of governing, procedural, test, and measured-outcome documents, and build a separate capsule-aware evidence-selection pilot. Preserve the frozen TASK-261 selector and TASK-260/TASK-261 results byte-for-byte. Use known queries only as labeled development data, measure exact-source visibility and context, record temporal/staleness risks, and do not integrate capsules into startup, canonical authority, routing, UI, embeddings, external services, or every Markdown file.
acceptance_criteria: The capsule convention is human-readable, 60-120 words, uses required Purpose/Proves/Applies to/Does not provide/Evidence type/Status fields, and explicitly remains descriptive metadata rather than authority.

A parser and validator reject duplicate capsules, missing/unknown fields, invalid evidence types/status values, excessive length, and empty boundaries while leaving documents without capsules valid fallbacks.
At least six representative Markdown documents receive capsules via additive edits only; existing body prose is preserved and each capsule states limitations or non-authority boundaries.

A separate capsule-aware pilot leaves TASK-261 code/tests/results byte-for-byte unchanged, allocates at most three query-global sources, records capsule-vs-fallback provenance, and compares exact-source visibility with the recorded 16/20 known-development result.

Focused tests cover parsing, validation, no-capsule fallback, role/boundary scoring, deterministic allocation, and stale/current attribution; the report documents benefits, authoring cost, staleness risk, negative-query implications, and a fresh-holdout recommendation without integration or embedding claims.
